title: Simultaneous Intensity and Frequency Control for Optical Waveform Generation using an Acousto Optic Modulator
authors: Hariprasad Madathil, Shengzhi Wang, F. Elohim Becerra
abstract: We describe a method for calibrating the response of an acousto-optic modulator (AOM) to enable precise, arbitrary control of the intensity and frequency of optical fields. The method involves characterizing the nonlinear response of the AOM to its input RF drive voltage and applying an iterative calibration/correction algorithm to accurately map input RF amplitude and frequency drive to output optical intensity and frequency shifts. After a few calibration/correction iterations, the calibration of the AOM maintains the optical power within 1$\%$ of a constant target value over relatively wide frequency tuning range ($\approx$100 MHz), with $σ=0.2\%$ relative deviation. We apply this calibration method to generate programmable waveforms and optical pulses with tailored intensity and frequency profiles that closely match their target specifications. This technique offers a simple and robust method for applications that require high-accuracy optical modulation.
summary: This paper presents a novel, calibration-based method to achieve simultaneous, high-accuracy control over both the intensity and frequency of light generated by an Acousto-Optic Modulator (AOM). By employing an iterative correction algorithm, the authors compensate for the AOM's inherent nonlinear response. This allows for the generation of complex, programmable optical waveforms with unprecedented stability and precision.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving precise, arbitrary simultaneous control over both the intensity and frequency of an optical field generated using an Acousto-Optic Modulator (AOM).
main_result: The authors developed an iterative calibration method that successfully maintains optical power within 1% of a constant target value over a wide frequency tuning range ($\approx 100$ MHz).
method: The technique involves characterizing the AOM's nonlinear response to its RF drive voltages and applying an iterative correction algorithm to map input voltages accurately to desired output intensity and frequency shifts.
model_or_system: The system utilizes an Acousto-Optic Modulator (AOM) driven by controlled RF voltages ($V_{AM}$ and $V_{FM}$) to modulate an optical field. The control is achieved through iterative compensation rather than relying on a detailed physical model.
key_observables: Output optical intensity ($I$), output optical field frequency ($\omega_{out}$), and the relative standard deviation ($\sigma$) of the intensity.
important_parameters: Frequency tuning range ($\approx 100$ MHz), relative intensity deviation ($\sigma \approx 0.2\%$), and the required number of calibration iterations (up to fourteen).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that the AOM's nonlinear response can be characterized experimentally and compensated for iteratively, avoiding the need for a full physical model.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the general AOM setup, the iterative compensation process (showing intensity stabilization), and the successful generation of complex waveforms (e.g., Gaussian intensity with frequency sweeps) in both single-pass and double-pass configurations.
paper_structure: The paper details the problem of AOM nonlinearity, proposes an iterative calibration methodology involving inverse function mapping, demonstrates the procedure using experimental setups, and applies the technique to generate complex, tailored optical waveforms.
why_interesting: This work provides a robust, hardware-based technique for high-precision optical waveform generation, which is crucial for advanced quantum optics experiments requiring stable, tunable light sources.
